findings.claim: Remember large integer values from earlier chunks before promoting a numeric column to double precision.
evidence: e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b:research_cloud/sqlimport/load_inputs.py:137-166 processes 50,000-row chunks. A bigint chunk with 9007199254740993 takes the ints.all() continue branch; a later fractional value promotes the column to double precision, and the exact-integer check examines only that later chunk.

e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b:research_cloud/sqlimport/load_inputs.py:169-174 and e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b:research_cloud/sqlimport/load_inputs.py:237-249 then convert source and SQL values to the same rounded float during comparison, so the loss is invisible to the verifier.

Confirmed against audited_sha in disposable PostgreSQL: CSV value column containing 9007199254740993, followed by 49,999 rows of 1, then 0.5 imported as double precision. The first SQL value was 9007199254740992.0, but load_one returned verified with all 50,001 cells compared and no mismatches. Exact output is in /tmp/4b7c22-pg-tests.log (SHA256 f69c89ee38bd3758b1322d15c374c939210c6a6960b24b1c10f1165da8be90a1).

e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b:.trellis/tasks/10-16-gcp-research-modeling-migration/design.md:52-52 requires validating numeric roundtrips. e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b:research_cloud/tests/test_sqlimport.py:70-87 covers a mixed large integer/fractional column within one chunk, so it misses the cross-chunk case.
findings.impact: A mixed numeric source column can silently lose integer precision depending on row order and still receive a verified import receipt. Identifier columns are separately kept as text and immutable source files remain available; this audit did not establish that the migrated corpus contains the triggering values. The confirmed defect is therefore limited to this import edge case rather than a demonstrated corruption of current scientific outputs.
findings.remediation: Carry each column's integer precision constraints across all chunks, and retain text when any observed integer cannot safely enter a later floating-point column. Add a cross-CHUNK-boundary roundtrip test, in both row orders, that checks the original integer before any float conversion.

limitations: Scope is the supplied two-endpoint task diff and demonstrated dependencies. No prior audit reports were supplied or reused. Older scientific source trees, unrelated operational workflows and the full historical experiment/acceptance matrix were not re-audited.

GitNexus list_repos returned no exact-case match for the supplied gitnexus_repo. Its IPCCH_operational entry used the differently cased source path and lastCommit 8feec3a113829364483e226e4ef56ec66227a183 (177 commits behind reported HEAD), not audited_sha. Used bounded pinned-source reads instead; did not reindex or mutate either checkout.

Cloud state was assessed from committed receipts and explicit source/dependency checks, not refreshed through external services. No paid calls, cloud jobs, installation, executor transcripts, sub-agents or Trellis state changes were used. The only external-dependency expansions were the installed MLflow CLI/tool-executor semantics and archived P6 loader needed by the changed callers/tests.

The live assistant deny probe was a model self-refusal and did not execute a prohibited tool. Static allowlist/dependency inspection, startup checks and local guard tests support the scoped conclusion; no live adversarial provider call was made.

The accepted historical HPT attempt ran before the external timeout correction and never reached its per-trial cap. Current code/admission tests cover the corrected wrapper; no new paid HPT run was launched. Billing actuals remain unavailable, and the recorded estimates, post-hoc reservations and unrelated-project exclusions are not a project-wide spending guarantee.

The first focused suite attempt used the read-only clone as cwd and failed its local MLflow fixture because the default artifact directory needed a writable working directory. Repeating the unchanged tests with cwd=/tmp passed. An initial Bubblewrap mount at /repo also failed before tests because the host root was read-only; the successful sandbox uses /tmp/repo. These audit-runner setup errors were not treated as implementation findings.

The existing CSV receipt checks were reconciled, but the 13.76 GB source corpus was not rescanned to determine whether A01 occurred historically. Raw/source bytes were not changed. Scratch logs live in /tmp and may be ephemeral; the reproduction and hashes are retained in this result.
Both the frozen audit repository and independent test clone remained clean at audited_sha after verification. No repair was made; the controller owns disposition of the finding.
result.summary: Controller-close diff-first audit of 99d390b7df536ba8d2661b94a80f29d5abac09fd..e0a3b4521799a254380b4ef68e5969be76c3564b: the new research_cloud integration and directly linked migration, access, training, package and cutover evidence. review_base_sha equals base_sha; review-scope.json contains no prior reports or unresolved prior findings, so no prior audit acceptance was inferred. One minor data-integrity defect is confirmed: cross-chunk numeric type inference can round a previously read large integer while reporting a verified SQL import. Ninety-two focused tests passed (49 service/admission/transfer tests, 27 PostgreSQL tests, 16 package/IPCCH boundary tests), and a separate 50,001-row fixture reproduced the defect. The stored 242-version registry and 223-package publication/download/replay chain reconcile. This is a scoped change review, not a new certification of every historical experiment or the live cloud deployment.
